dowdy

DOW-dee · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Dowdy is unfashionable and drab in appearance, especially in clothing.

The costume designer intentionally dressed the schoolteacher character in dowdy cardigans to contrast with the flashy lead actress.

Example

The once-trendy shopping mall now looked dowdy, its faded signs and outdated storefronts untouched since the 1990s.

Nothing about the mall was stylish or up to date anymore -- it looked drab and old-fashioned, exactly what dowdy describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

frumpy: Frumpy describes a person who looks dumpy and out of style in what they are wearing — it is almost always said of someone. Dowdy makes the same judgment but ranges wider: a cardigan, a hotel lobby, or a train station can look dowdy without anyone in the picture.

drab: Drab is strictly about color and brightness — dull, gray, cheerless, with nothing to catch the eye. Dowdy folds fashion into the judgment: dowdy clothes are not just dull but noticeably out of date. A brand-new gray uniform is drab; a cut from decades ago is dowdy.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

chic: stylish and fashionable

stylish: having a fashionable, attractive design

Where it sits · how run-down the look is

plain → dowdy → shabby

plain vs. dowdy: Something plain is simply simple and unadorned — a milder look than dowdy, which adds the sense of being drab and out of fashion.

shabby vs. dowdy: Something shabby is worn-out and threadbare from use — a more run-down look than dowdy, whose clothes can be perfectly neat and still look dated.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — dowd: a plain, dully dressed person (an obsolete word) (Middle English, origin uncertain)

suffix — -y: having the quality of (English)

Put it together: Dowdy's exact origin is genuinely uncertain -- dictionaries trace it only as far back as an obsolete word 'dowd,' used for a plain, dully dressed woman, with no clear root beyond that.

Use the root in a new word: dowd: Old etiquette guides sometimes warned young women against becoming a 'dowd' who never bothered with fashion.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Dowdy is about being unfashionable and drab, not necessarily untidy -- clothing can be perfectly neat and clean and still look dowdy, which sets it apart from unkempt (messy and uncared for) or tousled (playfully disordered).
